contract: solve(a, b) -> permutation p of 0..n-1 (list of n integers); a and b are this task's QAPLIB matrices (int64 NumPy arrays of shape (n, n), first and second matrix of the instance file, passed as copies). Facility i is placed at location p[i]. Score: the exact integer cost sum_{i,j} a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]], minimized. The instance file is read from the prepared data directory and its SHA-256 is checked before every evaluation.
notes: Independent exact objective in the QAPLIB convention (first matrix indexed by facilities, second by locations). The published record construction for every task was scored with this evaluator and reproduces the published value exactly (validation/human-results/frontier_combinatorics.json). Instances and best known solutions come from the QAPLIB deposit on Edinburgh DataShare (CC BY 4.0); the instance files are fetched by scripts/prepare_frontier_combinatorics.py and pinned by SHA-256. Unit tests compare the objective with brute force on small instances.
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Quadratic assignment: QAPLIB tho150
description: Assign the 150 facilities of the QAPLIB instance tho150 to 150 locations so that the sum of flow times distance is as small as possible. The best known assignment costs 8,133,398 and no optimality proof exists.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: QAPLIB deposit (CC BY 4.0): tho150.dat in qapdata.tar.gz (SHA-256 40136bc14aa404f9...) and the best known permutation tho150.sln in qapsoln.tar.gz; the README table lists 8133398 for tho150.
Burkard, Karisch and Rendl (1997), QAPLIB - a quadratic assignment problem library: instance definitions and conventions.

limitations: QAPLIB lists the triangle-decomposition lower bound 7,620,628 (gap 6.30%).
The instance file is fetched by scripts/prepare_frontier_combinatorics.py and pinned by SHA-256; the evaluator refuses a file with another digest.

The record construction is public, so a candidate can reproduce the record by embedding it; the score measures the returned object, not the search that produced it, and only a strictly smaller score than the best known value is a new result.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process as trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes every property of the returned object exactly and trusts nothing the candidate reports.

state_of_the_art.statement: The best known solution of Thonemann and Boelte's instance tho150 with rectangular distances costs 8,133,398; it was found by simulated annealing (QAPLIB code SIM-3, A. Misevicius, Informatica 2003) and is recorded in QAPLIB. QAPLIB lists the triangle-decomposition lower bound 7,620,628 (gap 6.30%). No later improvement was found in the literature reviewed on 2026-10-12.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a minimum-cost Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment of facilities to locations for the QAPLIB instance tho150.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The quadratic assignment problem models facility and hospital layout, keyboard design, backboard wiring and turbine balancing. It is NP-hard and notoriously difficult in practice: QAPLIB instances above about 40 facilities remain unsolved, and the best known solutions of the large instances have resisted improvement for decades, so a cheaper permutation is a new best known solution of a standard open instance.
